clue.text: Miso soup contains one calorie and is an art!

indicators.note: contains says the jumbled letters hold another piece within them
soup suggests ingredients stirred together, so the letters of miso are mixed up

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article
C is the standard abbreviation for a calorie

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a bowl of miso soup, with its calorie, counts as a work of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soup' rearranges MISO to MOSI, which 'contains' A; C follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Mosaic is a decorative craft of setting small tiles into patterns, an art form.

clue.text: A measure of fine vodka served up for baker

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means the letters rise, reading bottom to top
a measure of takes only a portion of the words fine vodka, as a tot is part of a bottle

explanation.surface: Someone pours a fine vodka measure for the person who makes the bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A measure of' takes NEVO from 'fine vodka'; 'served up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A baker is something that bakes, and an oven is the appliance that does the baking.

clue.text: Not feeling pain in part of alimentary canal that is gas-generated

indicators.note: part of takes a stretch of letters from inside the word canal
generated means produced afresh, so the letters are rearranged into new order

parts.note: that is translates to IE, the abbreviation of id est

explanation.surface: A medical note about gas made in the gut and its effect on feeling pain.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a digestive complaint; the indicator 'generated' does the rearranging, and the hyphen hides that 'gas' is fodder rather than description.
explanation.definitionFit: Analgesia is the medical term for absence of sensitivity to pain, as produced by painkillers.

clue.text: Vegetable often eaten raw, so it must be chopped in haste

indicators.note: must be chopped in tells us to cut the word it out of the synonym for haste

parts.note: celerity is a formal word for speed or haste
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice that a salad vegetable needs chopping quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be chopped in' removes IT from CELERITY, leaving CELERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Celery is a crunchy salad vegetable whose stalks are commonly eaten uncooked.

clue.text: Culinary instructions from Dr John?

parts.note: to doctor accounts is to cook them, falsify them
John is a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: Asks whether a recipe collection might come from a physician named John.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr looks like a title for John but is the verb 'doctor', to falsify; John is the Gospel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cookbook is a volume of recipes, which are instructions for preparing food.

clue.text: Sweet, hot sauce cools me, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly hints at an unexpected outcome, so the letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone finds, to their surprise, that a hot sauce cools them down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges all fifteen letters of HOT SAUCE COOLS ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate mousse is a light whipped dessert, and a sweet is the British name for a dessert course.

clue.text: Dismissed waiters carry these, content to await posting

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
waiters bring food and drinks on trays

explanation.surface: Sacked waiters and their trays, with a hint at mail waiting to be sent.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the desk containers by their contents: letters waiting to be sent.
explanation.definitionFit: Out trays are office containers holding finished correspondence that is waiting to be sent out.

clue.text: Support conservation of kingfish

indicators.note: conservation of means keeping something safe inside, so the support holds the next piece

parts.note: a beam is a structural support
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A call to back protection of a large sea fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kingfish' looks like one word to define, but splits: king gives R, fish is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bream is a common name for several freshwater and sea fish.

clue.text: More than compensate for inaccurate scales?

parts.note: a figure that is out is wrong or inaccurate
scales are a balance, a weighing instrument

explanation.surface: Asks whether faulty scales could overcorrect.
explanation.definitionFit: To outbalance is to outweigh, exceeding in weight or importance what it is set against.

clue.text: Bubbly galore is found in women's quarters

indicators.note: bubbly suggests fizzing and effervescing, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Champagne flowing freely in a harem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bubbly' looks like champagne but rearranges GALORE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio is the secluded apartments for wives and concubines in a Muslim palace, a harem.

clue.text: Cardinal downing half of Australian beer

definitions.meaning: a cardinal number is a counting number such as one, two, three
the Queensland lager Fourex is written XXXX, and half of those Roman numerals is XX

explanation.surface: A churchman drinks half a can of Australian lager.
explanation.walkthrough: XXXX (Fourex) is an Australian beer; half of it is XX, Roman twenty. 'downing' links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty is a counting number, and cardinal numbers are the ones used for counting.

clue.text: Roar my gonads off, being a chef

indicators.note: off means gone bad or awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A coarse exclamation about a famously foul-mouthed kitchen figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges ROAR MY GONADS. Gordon Ramsay is a British TV chef known for swearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gordon Ramsay is a celebrity Scottish chef with many restaurants and TV shows.

clue.text: Johnny may, perhaps, find source of milky liquid

parts.note: johnny is British slang for a condom, also called a rubber
may is hawthorn, an example of a tree, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: A man called Johnny may, perhaps, find where a white liquid comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: Johnny and May look like names or a verb; they are a condom and the hawthorn.
explanation.definitionFit: The rubber tree yields latex, a white milky sap tapped for making rubber.

clue.text: Make messy hummus salad sandwich

indicators.note: a sandwich holds a filling between slices, so the answer is enclosed by the words

explanation.surface: A hummus salad sandwich has been made a mess of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwich' looks like food but holds the letters within 'hummus salad'.
explanation.definitionFit: To muss is to rumple or disarrange, as with hair or clothes.

clue.text: Unusual, unnatural craving for food in Italy leaving one puzzled

indicators.note: in places the craving inside the jumbled remainder
puzzled means confused, so the remaining letters are jumbled
leaving says one piece departs from the word Italy

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
pica is the medical term for an appetite for non-food substances

explanation.surface: An odd hunger strikes someone in Italy, leaving them baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: Indicators: 'leaving' drops one letter, 'puzzled' jumbles what remains of the country into ATYL, and 'in' sets the craving within. Pica is a medical term, fair but unfamiliar to many.
explanation.definitionFit: Atypical means not representative of the type, hence unusual or irregular.

clue.text: Cooked meat and veg in stock in Sligo?

definitions.text: Cooked meat and veg in stock in Sligo?

parts.words: Cooked meat and veg in stock in Sligo?
parts.note: a slow-cooked dish of meat and vegetables simmered in liquid, as made in an Irish county town

explanation.surface: Describes a meal of meat and vegetables simmered in liquid in a town in western Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Sligo is a town and county in the west of Ireland; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish stew is a traditional dish of mutton, potatoes and onions simmered in broth.

clue.text: Baker's dozen + 5 = 10-2

parts.note: a baker's dozen is thirteen, plus five; 10-2 is the number at 10 across less two

explanation.surface: An arithmetic sum mixing bakery counts and grid references.
explanation.walkthrough: A baker's dozen is thirteen, a baker giving an extra loaf; 10 across is TWENTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirteen plus five, or twenty minus two, both equal the number after seventeen.

clue.text: Annoying American warrior concealed ingredient vital for chips

indicators.note: concealed says the warrior hides the next piece within

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior
Si is the chemical symbol for silicon, the material of computer chips

explanation.surface: An irritating US fighter has hidden a key element of fried potatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chips' suggests fried potatoes; they are microchips, made of silicon.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasive describes a harsh, grating manner that rubs people up the wrong way.

clue.text: Failing to start to get rid of hunger

indicators.note: failing to start means the first letter is missing

parts.note: to ditch something is to get rid of it

explanation.surface: Advice to remove a craving before it begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing to start' drops the D from DITCH.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless craving or longing, as in an itch to travel.

clue.text: Old Mediterranean geezer knocked back chopped onion stuffing

indicators.note: stuffing says the turned letters fill the inside of the man

parts.note: geezer is British slang for a man

indicators.note: knocked back means turned round, reading the letters in reverse
chopped means cut short, so the end of onion goes

explanation.surface: An old fellow downs a stuffing made of chopped onion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped' cuts ONION to ONI; 'knocked back' turns it to INO, 'stuffing' MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Minoan refers to the Bronze Age civilisation of Crete, in the ancient Mediterranean.

clue.text: What the Roux brothers brought to the table?

definitions.text: What the Roux brothers brought to the table?

parts.words: What the Roux brothers brought to the table?
parts.note: read as a glossy finish applied to wooden furniture, rather than the cooking of two famous chefs from France

explanation.surface: Asks what two celebrated chefs contributed to dining.
explanation.walkthrough: Albert and Michel Roux were French chefs in London; the table is literal furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: French polish is a shellac finish that gives wooden furniture a high gloss.

clue.text: Island producing coconuts, nitrogen and a couple of metals

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
Ru is the chemical symbol for ruthenium

explanation.surface: A Pacific island exports coconuts, nitrogen and some metals.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauru is a small Pacific island nation where coconut palms grow.

clue.text: Invert bowl over bananas

indicators.note: invert means turn upside down, so in a down entry the letters run upwards

parts.note: to bowl someone over is to stun them

explanation.surface: Instructions to tip a bowl upside down over some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit but means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bananas and nuts are both informal words for mad or crazy.

clue.text: Carp and game

definitions.meaning: to carp is to complain or grumble
game birds are wild birds shot for sport, such as the red one of Scottish moors

explanation.surface: A fish and a game, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To grouse is to complain, and the grouse is a game bird shot in Britain.

clue.text: Type of pastry crust regularly used to save time

parts.note: short pastry, or shortcrust, is a crumbly pastry

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word crust

explanation.surface: A pastry cook uses a particular crust to work faster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes C, U, T from 'crust'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortcut is a quicker method or route, something adopted to cut down time spent.

clue.text: Order a course

definitions.meaning: order as in the arrangement or succession of things
a course as in a series of events or a run of cards following one another

explanation.surface: Ordering a course in a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequence is an ordered succession, and a course can mean a connected series.

clue.text: Born craving mint? Not quite!

parts.note: né is French for born, used in English of a man's original name
a wish is a desire or craving

explanation.surface: A newborn yearns for a mint, or almost does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mint' looks like a sweet but means brand new, as in mint condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nearly in mint condition is fairly new but not quite brand new.
